content.content:
#### Attachments

What is attached to the prompt is listed above the text input, between the tabs and the input, one row per attachment in the order they were attached, and only while there is anything attached. An attached piece of text shows a quote icon, the text's first line cut off with an ellipsis, and, when it runs to more than one line, how many lines it has, muted, and at the right end a small button with a cross, whose tooltip says it removes the attachment, which removes just that one.
Images can be attached too: pasted from the clipboard while the chat input has focus, dropped onto the chat input from the file manager, or chosen with a small ghost button with an image icon, whose tooltip says "Attach images", on the tab row between the last tab and the help text, which opens the platform's file picker for any files, several at once, since the picker can't be limited to images. Pasting an image attaches it rather than putting anything in the text, even when the clipboard holds text as well; every image on the clipboard is attached, and a clipboard with no image pastes its text as usual. Several files dropped or chosen at once are attached in their order, each on its own merits. An image is known by its content, not its name, and only PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP are taken: anything else pasted, dropped, or chosen, BMP, TIFF, and SVG included, is not attached, and a warning notification titled "Not attached" says it isn't an image. An image larger than 5 MB is not attached either, and the same notification says it is too large. A folder dropped or chosen isn't an image either, and a file that can't be read is not attached, the same notification saying it couldn't be read, and why. Each file left out has its own notification, and the others are still attached.
Files can be dropped only on the chat input itself, its tabs, the attachments, and the text input; dropping them on the message list above it does nothing. While files are dragged over the chat input, its background is highlighted with the accent's fill, laid about a quarter of the way over it.
An attached image's row shows a small thumbnail, its file name, or "Pasted image" for one pasted, and its size in pixels, muted, with the same remove button; hovering the thumbnail shows the image larger, at most 320 pixels. Images and text are listed together in the order they were attached while the prompt is written. A prompt taken back into the input, as when a queued prompt is edited, lists its text first, then its images, each image named by its saved file, a pasted one included.
Attachments belong to the prompt being written, not to a tab: switching tabs keeps them all, and they go with the prompt whichever tab it is sent from. When the prompt is sent, its attachments are sent along with it and the list empties, as the text input does. A queued prompt keeps the attachments it was sent with.

#### Projects
##### Attached Images

Each attached image is saved in the project's data, as the [ProjectDataScope](../../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, once the prompt is sent or queued, and a prompt with images gives the hidden anchor an attachedImages

###### Property

a list of the saved images' paths, from the project

directory, in the order they were attached, keyed image1, image2, and so on, each written as an escape block as attached text is. The same image attached twice is saved once but listed, and given to the harness, twice. The images themselves are never put into the compiled prompt as text. The preview draws its thumbnails from the images in memory, saving nothing.
The harness is given the images alongside the compiled prompt, in the way it takes images, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, in the order they were attached. A message sent to a running task can carry images the same way, and so can a question. A saved image that can't be found when the run starts fails it saying so, before anything is run.
Wherever an attached prompt is shown, in the latest task's header, among the previous tasks, in the questions of the Ask conversation, in the queue, and in the preview, its images are shown as thumbnails beneath the prompt as typed, between it and any slices, except in the latest task's header, where they come beneath the whole prompt, slices included. A message sent to a running task shows none in the task's output. The raw prompt lists their paths, as the [PromptEditor](../index.md#prompt-editor) says. Clicking a thumbnail opens the image full size, in the platform's image viewer. Resending, sending to the other mode, and editing a queued prompt keep its images, and a Freeform prompt sends them as any other does.
What the harness receives is the compiled userPrompt followed by the attached text: a line reading "Attached text:", then each piece as a fenced code block, whose fence is longer than any run of backticks in the text itself. This is also the compiled prompt shown in the task's header.

##### New Conversation

content.text:
Any file can now be attached to a prompt, not just images. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 82 files.

- **Attaching:** paste, drop or pick files the same way as images. The button is now a paperclip, "Attach files", and files copied in your file manager paste as attachments.
- **Images vs files:**
  - PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP up to 5 MB still go to the harness as images.
  - Anything else up to 25 MB is attached as a file, including other image formats and images over 5 MB, which used to be refused.
  - Folders and files over 25 MB are refused with a notification.
- **Rows:** each file shows a kind icon, its name and its size.
- **Saving:** files are saved in a new `.suspense/attachments/` folder, in subfolders named by time and content hash. Each prompt's hidden anchor lists them in a new `attachedFiles` property.
- **What the harness gets:** an "Attached files:" list of paths, names and sizes after any attached text, never the files' contents. The harness reads them with its own tools.
- **Containers:** container runs get each attached file mounted read only on its own, never the whole folder.
- **Showing and carrying:** wherever a prompt is shown, its files are listed, and clicking one opens it. Files travel with resends, sends to the other mode, edits of queued prompts, chain steps, questions and messages sent to a running task.

The 25 MB limit is my choice; I can change it.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `ChatInputScope` `#attachments` and `#attached-files`, `ProjectDataScope` `#contents`, and `ContainerEnvironmentScope` `#mounts`.
